title: Tactical launch runner — daily slate & rapid retro
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the operational runner for the upcoming feature drop window (targeting a phased push across regions). It is intentionally terse — meant for the launch conductor and on-call engineers to run a compact daily cadence and record rapid retros.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: API surface change (new route /v2/stream), one small model config tweak (kv-cache sizing), deploys to hosted and dedicated pools.
- Constraint: No DB schema changes. Canary only for 72 hours with automated throttle at token latency drift > 25%.
- Rollback must be possible within 6 minutes for hosted tier, 10 minutes for dedicated.

Daily slate (run by Launch Conductor):
- 06:00 PT — Preflight check (owner: on-call SRE)
  - Confirm infra green (k8s nodes, autoscaler pods running), CPU/GPU capacity >= planned reserve.
  - Quick smoke: /healthz on control plane, sample generation on canary instance (3 tokens, 200ms target).
  - Telemetry sanity: ingestion pipeline lag < 30s, token-rate sampling OK.
- 08:30 PT — Stakeholder sync (15m)
  - Attendees: Product PM, Release Conductor, SRE lead, Serving runtime lead, Observability engineer.
  - Agenda: status, blockers, canary ramp plan, rollback readiness.
- 10:00 PT — Canary throttle and observability sweep (owner: serving-runtime eng)
  - Start 1% traffic -> 5% over 30m if latency and error budget OK.
  - Verify KV cache hit rate, p50/p95 token latency, memory usage per replica.
- 12:00 PT — Midday check (owner: on-call SRE)
  - Run annotated smoke test suite (sample prompts + regression classifier).
  - Check for function-calling regressions (tooling hook tests).
- 14:00 PT — Canaries to 25% if green (owner: release-engineering)
  - Confirm rollout can autoscale without queueing.
- 17:00 PT — Evening stabilization check (owner: product infra)
  - Decision call: continue ramp or pause. If paused, trigger rollback readiness checklist.
- 22:00 PT — Night cap (owner: on-call SRE)
  - Ensure long-tail metrics stable; leave annotated summary for next morning.

Preflight checklist (run once, D-2 to D-1):
- Configuration
  - Validate config parity across envs (prod/dedicated test mirror).
  - Secret rotation status: KMS keys verified, HSM access test passed.
- Testing
  - Integration smoke: streaming endpoints + tool-calls validated on staging.
  - Load rehearsal: 10% synthetic traffic at target sequence length distribution.
- Observability
  - Dashboards templated, alerting rules in place (see linked telemetry doc).
  - Log retention window set to 7d for launch window.
- Rollback plan
  - Pre-signed rollback PR created and verified (PR#7821).
  - Fallback model variant (quantized v1) staged for immediate routing.

Rollback decision matrix (fast-mode):
- Trigger immediate rollback if any of:
  - Error rate delta > 2% absolute for 15m (end user 5xx rate).
  - p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline for 10m.
  - Severe functional regression detected by regression classifier (precision > 90%).
- If trigger fired:
  - Notify channel #launch-runner and page SRE on-call.
  - Execute rollback PR: disable new route traffic, route to fallback model variant, scale down new replicas.
  - Start incident doc and tag 'rollback' and 'rapid-retro'.

Rollout calendar (compact):
- Day -2 (2026-09-20): preflight dry run, health checks, rollout rehearsals at 50% load.
- Day -1 (2026-09-21): config freeze, golden-snapshot created, final canary artifacts produced.
- Day 0  (2026-09-22): Canary start 01:00 UTC (1% -> 5% -> 25% per schedule), midday cross-checks, evening decision.
- Day +1 (2026-09-23): Expand to 50% if green, increase observability retention.
- Day +2 (2026-09-24): Full ramp for hosted; dedicated mirror rollouts follow staggered regional windows.
- Day +7 (2026-09-29): Post-rollout regression sweep and metric stability signoff.

Launch-specific telemetry thresholds (quick references):
- Token latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms (sequence length median).
- Error budget: 99.5% success calls (no 5xx) per 1h window during canary.
- KV cache hit target: >= 65% for optimization routes.
- Ingestion lag for observability: < 45s.

Rapid retro template (filled nightly):
- Date:
- Short summary (3 lines):
- What went well (bulleted):
- What tripped us (bulleted):
- Immediate follow-ups (owner + ETA):
- Signals to watch tomorrow:

Example quick entry (2026-09-22):
- Date: 2026-09-22
- Short summary: Canary progressed to 25% by 14:30 PT, p95 stable, small spike in tool-call time at 11:40 -> rolled back that micro config.
- What went well:
  - Autoscaler responded within thresholds, observed no queueing.
  - Observability alert fired and page correctly routed.
- What tripped us:
  - One micro-config (kv-cache size) caused function-call tail increase; we reverted micro-change and re-ramped.
- Immediate follow-ups:
  - Add runtime guard to reject cache size > X (Priya, 2026-09-24).
  - Add a synthetic regression that targets function-calls (Liam, 2026-09-23).
- Signals to watch tomorrow:
  - Function-call p99, tool-call time distribution, memory churn per replica.

Release notes (draft — include in customer-facing bulletin after final sign-off):
- Headline: Faster streaming for v2 endpoints; reduced tail latency for common prompts.
- Notable changes:
  1) Added new streaming route /v2/stream with improved prefix caching.
  2) Optimized KV-cache defaults for smaller prompt families (saves ~7% token cost).
  3) Observability: added token-level trace IDs to all streaming responses (helps debugging).
- Impact for customers:
  - Minimal API surface change (new route). Existing /v1 routes unaffected.
  - Default model behavior will be slightly more cache-friendly; edge cases where customers tuned kv-cache manually may see slightly different latency profiles.
- Known issues (to communicate internally; hide until fixed):
  - Rare function-call tail increases observed under certain prompt shapes (mitigation: staged fallback to quantized variant).
  - Some legacy SDK versions will not auto-discover /v2/stream; SDKs need a minor patch (PR in progress).

Post-launch checklist (D+0 to D+7):
- D+0: Confirm final canary telemetry and send internal memo.
- D+1: Run full regression harness and surface top 5 anomalies.
- D+3: Stakeholder review meeting and decision whether to mark release final.
- D+7: Product sign-off and customer-facing release notes go live.

Notes for the conductor:
- Keep entries short and time-stamped. If you perform a technical mitigation, attach the rollback PR or artifact id in the rapid retro entry.
- If an alert pages, escalate immediately according to the rollback decision matrix; do not wait for stakeholder sync.

Open questions (capture during ops):
- Do we want an automated preflight gate that rejects canary if median sequence length deviates > 25% from historical? (suggested: yes, add to D-2 rehearsal).
- Should SDKs perform implicit discovery of /v2/stream during rollout window? (risk: confusion with older client versions).

Appendix (quick links):
- Regression harness: confluence:tests/regression-harness-2026
- Telemetry doc: docs/observability/telemetry-signals-2026
- Rollback PR: PR#7821

END OF RUNNER
